item.title: FastMCP 3.2 Adds AI‑Assisted Search to Calibre Library
item.description:
FastMCP 3.2 Adds AI‑Assisted Search to Calibre Library

FastMCP 3.2 extends Calibre e‑book library with AI‑assisted search, RAG, and agentic workflows.

🔍 Overview

  • AI‑assisted search, Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG), and agentic workflows for Sandra’s 1000+ book library.
  • Exposes 33 portmanteau tools for natural‑language library management.
  • Built into Calibre’s core engine.

🧩 How it works

  • Bridges Calibre e‑book library and AI assistants (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.) via the Model Context Protocol.
  • Reads Calibre’s metadata.db directly and indexes metadata for semantic search using LanceDB.
  • Provides Incremental LanceDB RAG Sync and Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) hybrid search.
  • Offers a 21‑tool registry and a portmanteau CRUD & Library Health Engine.

⚙️ Key details

  • FastMCP 3.2 Server (port :10720) and WebApp (Next.js 15 on :10721).
  • Calibre GUI + Plugin (Qt6 / PyQt5).
  • FastAPI REST layer with async background workers.
  • CALIBRE CONTENT SERVER (e.g., :8099, http://goliath:8099/ or http://localhost:8080/).
  • Async Python Engine (calibre.srv) and RapydScript SPA (index-generated.html).
  • HTML5 In‑Browser Reader (viewer.js / offline SW) and OPDS Mobile Catalog Feed.
  • Databases: metadata.db (Calibre SQLite catalog), full-text-search.db (FTS5 token index), calibre_mcp_data.db (sidecar extended metadata).
  • Semantic search powered by LanceDB, fastembed (BAAI/bge-small), and Ollama/OpenAI providers.

🚀 Availability

  • Download Calibre MCP_*_x64-setup.exe from Releases, double‑click to launch Calibre MCP.
  • Claude Desktop one‑liner: download calibre‑mcp.mcpb from Releases and install via Settings → MCP Servers → Install from file.
  • After installation, use prompts such as “Find unread sci‑fi books”, “Open a random Banks novel”, or “What’s my library health?”.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides AI‑powered semantic search and natural‑language library management directly within Calibre.
  • Enables RAG and agentic workflows to help users navigate large e‑book collections efficiently.

#Calibre #AI #LanceDB #SemanticSearch #Python

Source: sandraschi/calibremcp

item.title: Haiku RAG Launches Open-Source Agentic Retrieval System with Docling and Ollama
item.description:
Haiku RAG Launches Open-Source Agentic Retrieval System with Docling and Ollama

A new open-source project called Haiku RAG has been released, offering an agentic retrieval-augmented generation system that answers questions about user documents with citations to page numbers and section headings. The system runs on an embedded LanceDB database with open models through Ollama by default, requiring no server or API key. It supports multiple providers via Pydantic AI, and the same database can live on S3, GCS, Azure, or LanceDB Cloud. Built on LanceDB, Pydantic AI, and Docling, it ingests PDFs, office documents, HTML, Markdown, and images. The stored DoclingDocument preserves headings, tables, pictures, and page provenance. Search utilizes hybrid vector and full-text retrieval, optional reranking with cross-encoders and various providers, section-aware context expansion, and image search with multimodal embedders. It can answer with RAG capability, searching, running sandboxed Python for counting and aggregation, and citing page numbers and headings. Vision models receive figures directly. Optional capabilities compact earlier evidence and require answers to declare grounding. Citations can be checked by drawing chunks on page images from CLI, chat TUI, or Python. Integration options include Python API, native Pydantic AI capabilities, plugin hooks, MCP server for Claude Code, Codex, and Claude Desktop, plus a reference web app. The haiku-ingester service supports filesystem, HTTP, S3, and WebDAV sources with a SQLite or Postgres job queue, control plane, dashboard, tags, rollback, vacuum, and health checks. Python 3.12 or newer is required. Installation offers two packages: pip install haiku.rag for full features including Docling, VoyageAI, Cohere embedders, all rerankers, and TUI; and pip install haiku.rag-slim for core with extras. Default configuration uses Ollama for embeddings and answers. Commands include haiku-rag init, haiku-rag add-src, haiku-rag search, haiku-rag ask, haiku-rag chat, and haiku-rag mcp --stdio. The ingester service runs separately with haiku-ingester serve and supports continuous ingestion from configured sources.

#AI #RAG #OpenSource #LLM #Docling #LanceDB

Source: ggozad/haiku.rag

item.title: LanceDB Provides Open Source and Enterprise Vector Search Options
item.description:
LanceDB Provides Open Source and Enterprise Vector Search Options

LanceDB has launched as a database designed for fast, scalable, and production-ready vector search. The system is built on the Lance columnar format, serving as a central location for developers to build, train, and analyze AI workloads while storing and indexing petabytes of multimodal data.

🔍 Overview

LanceDB supports comprehensive search capabilities, including vector similarity search, full-text search, and SQL. It allows users to store, query, and filter vectors, metadata, and multimodal data such as text, images, videos, and point clouds. The platform is engineered to search billions of vectors in milliseconds using state-of-the-art indexing.

🧩 How it works

The database is built on the Lance columnar format, which provides efficient storage and analytics. Advanced features include zero-copy operations and automatic versioning, allowing users to manage data versions without requiring extra infrastructure. The system also supports GPU usage in the process of building vector indexes.

⚙️ Key details

LanceDB is available in two primary configurations:

Version Description
LanceDB Embedded (open source) Runs in the application’s process; data resides on local disk or in object storage; 100% open source with no vendor lock-in.
LanceDB Enterprise Offers production-scale distributed search, indexing, and maintenance, plus complete data sovereignty and security.

🚀 Availability

Developers can integrate LanceDB through Python, Node.js, Rust, and REST APIs. Native support is provided for Python and JavaScript/TypeScript, with API and SDK support available for Python, TypeScript, and Rust.

#LanceDB #VectorSearch #Database #MultimodalAI
